record.paper_title: Open Problems on Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded domain in ℝⁿ, and let 0 < λ₁ < λ₂ ≤ λ₃ ≤ ··· be the Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian, defined by −Δu = λu in Ω with u = 0 on ∂Ω. Must the ratio (λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁)/λ₁ always be at most the corresponding value for the Euclidean n-ball, namely n j_{p+1,1}² / j_{p,1}² where p = (n−2)/2 and j_{ν,k} denotes the k-th positive zero of the Bessel function J_ν? In particular, for n = 2, is (λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁ ≤ ((λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁)_disk ≈ 5.077?

evidence.quote: For Ω ⊂ ℝ² show that (λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁ ≤ ((λ₂ + λ₃)/λ₁)|disk ≈ 5.077. In ℝⁿ this conjecture reads (λ₂ + ··· + λₙ₊₁)/λ₁ ≤ n j²_{p+1,1}/j²_{p,1}.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ ($n \ge 2$) be a bounded domain, and let
\[
0 < \lambda_1(\Omega) < \lambda_2(\Omega) \le \lambda_3(\Omega) \le \cdots
\]
denote the eigenvalues (counted with multiplicity) of the Dirichlet Laplacian on $\Omega$, i.e. the values $\lambda$ for which there exists a nonzero $u \in H^1_0(\Omega)$ with $-\Delta u = \lambda u$ in $\Omega$ and $u = 0$ on $\partial\Omega$.

For a real parameter $\nu \ge 0$, let $J_\nu$ denote the Bessel function of the first kind of order $\nu$, and let $j_{\nu,k}$ denote its $k$-th positive zero. Set $p = (n-2)/2$. It is known that, when $\Omega = B \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ is the Euclidean unit ball, the first eigenvalue equals $j_{p,1}^2$, while $\lambda_2(B) = \cdots = \lambda_{n+1}(B) = j_{p+1,1}^2$, so that
\[
\frac{\lambda_2(B) + \lambda_3(B) + \cdots + \lambda_{n+1}(B)}{\lambda_1(B)} = \frac{n\, j_{p+1,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2}.
\]

Prove or disprove: for every bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$,
\[
\frac{\lambda_2(\Omega) + \lambda_3(\Omega) + \cdots + \lambda_{n+1}(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)} \;\le\; \frac{n\, j_{p+1,1}^2}{j_{p,1}^2}.
\]
In particular, for $n = 2$, decide whether
\[
\frac{\lambda_2(\Omega) + \lambda_3(\Omega)}{\lambda_1(\Omega)} \;\le\; \frac{2\, j_{1,1}^2}{j_{0,1}^2} \;\approx\; 5.077
\]
holds for every bounded planar domain $\Omega$, with equality (in the limit) only for the disk.
artifact.status_search_result: The inequality is the Ashbaugh–Benguria PPW-type conjecture for the sum of the second through $(n+1)$-st Dirichlet eigenvalues divided by the first. Partial results exist (e.g., work on the Ashbaugh–Benguria conjecture about lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues, and PPW-type results in symmetric spaces), but the conjecture in its general form for arbitrary bounded domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$ (including the planar case with bound $\approx 5.077$) appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Ashbaugh-Benguria's Conjecture about Lower Order Dirichlet Eigenvalues of the Laplacian
status_evidence.snippet: Paper studies the Ashbaugh–Benguria conjecture on lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian; treats the conjecture as not fully resolved in general.
status_evidence.claim: The conjecture about the sum of lower-order Dirichlet eigenvalues over $\lambda_1$ being maximized by the ball remains an active conjecture with only partial progress.

status_evidence.title: On the PPW Conjecture for Hopf-Symmetric Sets in Non-compact Rank One Symmetric Space
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2025) work establishing PPW-type bounds in special symmetric settings, indicating the general PPW-type conjectures for eigenvalue ratios remain open in full generality.
status_evidence.claim: PPW-type conjectures for ratios of Dirichlet eigenvalues continue to be investigated, indicating they are still open in the general Euclidean setting.
